output.subject: We've received your complaint about collection calls
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for speaking with us and for explaining what has been happening. We know how hard it is to manage this while caring for a newborn, and we're sorry for the stress and disruption you've described.

We want to confirm that we have your complaint. As you told us:

- You have been receiving six to eight collection calls a day about your credit card.
- Some of these calls have come after 9pm, and one came at 7am on a Sunday.
- You mentioned that on 14 September you told the collector you would make a payment on the 15th, and the calls continued after that.
- You said the calls have been waking your baby.

You asked us to stop the collection calls and to send you written confirmation of any restrictions on when and how often you are contacted. We have noted both requests.

A specialist team is now reviewing your complaint, and we will respond to you within 10 business days.

Thank you again for taking the time to tell us about this.

Kind regards,

Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: Customer requested written confirmation of call restrictions; the draft does not confirm any restrictions. Decide whether to confirm what was noted on the account and include the specifics.
The representative noted the account as no calls before 8am or after 9pm, max 1 attempt/day. Verify this was applied and is in effect before referencing it.
Review the call logs to check the reported frequency (6-8/day) and timing (after 9pm, Sunday 7am).
Check whether the payment the customer said they would make on the 15th was received, and whether a payment arrangement was recorded.
Decide how to respond to the request to stop collection calls entirely, and whether to offer alternative contact methods.
Customer has a newborn; consider whether any hardship or vulnerability support applies.
Confirm the date of the customer's conversation with the collector (noted as 9/14) and the date format to use in the reply.
